course_description: This course, social issues, and professional practice, studies the social impact, implications, and effects of computers, and the responsibilities of computer professionals in directing the emerging technology. Its specific topic includes an overview of the history of computing, computer applications and their impact, the computing profession, the legal and ethical responsibilities of professionals and careers in computing.

course_learning_outcomes.text: understand the basic cultural, social, legal, and ethical issues inherent in the discipline of computing;
develop the ability to ask serious questions about the social impact of computing and to evaluate proposed answers to those questions;
evaluate the basic legal rights of software and hardware vendors and users, and to also appreciate the ethical values which are the basis of those rights;
facilitate the acquisition of knowledge concerning the pertinent social, ethical, legal, and professional issues in the realm of computing by immersing individuals in the broader societal context;

comprehend the responsibilities anticipated as future practitioners, and grasp the potential consequences of failure, acknowledging both personal limitations and the limitations of the tools employed;
demonstrate a commitment to staying abreast in their chosen specialization and broader discipline of computing over the long term and;
demonstrate 21st century skills in all learning activities.
To understand the basic cultural, social, legal, and ethical issues inherent in the discipline of computing.

To evaluate the basic legal rights of software and hardware vendors and users, and to also appreciate the ethical values which are the basis of those rights.
To exhibit 21st century skills in all learning activities showing proficiency and application at the highest level.
